Work in the reduction conventions of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]: $\gamma$ is the signature
$(+---)$ metric, $U$ the unit future timelike vector $U=n$, $r=\rho c^2$, the
frame $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is $\gamma$-orthonormal with $e_0=U$,
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}$ on spatial pairs, and indices are moved with
$\gamma$.

**(a) Schouten tensor.** The **reduction Schouten tensor** of $\gamma$ is
$$S_{ij}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ij}-\tfrac16S_\gamma\,\gamma_{ij},$$
where $\operatorname{Ric}$ and $S_\gamma=\gamma^{ab}\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}$ are
the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). If the dust field equation
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat\otimes U^\flat$ holds, then
$$S_{ij}=\kappa r\Bigl(U_iU_j-\tfrac13\gamma_{ij}\Bigr)-\tfrac13\Lambda\,\gamma_{ij}.$$
This normalization is fixed so that the standard Kulkarni--Nomizu decomposition
$$R_{ijkl}=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr)$$
holds for every metric of dimension four, with $C$ the Weyl tensor
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]); the identity is checked on
constant-curvature metrics in the Remarks.

**(b) Prescribed curvature.** The **prescribed curvature tensor** of a
configuration $(C,E,B,r)$ is the tensor field with frame components
$$R^{\mathrm{pre}}{}_{ijkl}:=C_{ijkl}+\tfrac12\bigl(S_{ik}\gamma_{jl}-S_{il}\gamma_{jk}+S_{jl}\gamma_{ik}-S_{jk}\gamma_{il}\bigr),\qquad S_{ij}\text{ as in (a)} ,$$
where $C=C[E,B]$ is the Weyl tensor reconstructed from the electric and
magnetic variables in (d). A **tentative reduced configuration** is a smooth assignment
$(e_a{}^\mu,\Gamma_a{}^i{}_j,E_{ij},B_{ij},r)$ in the gauge of
[[def-gr-dust-reduction-variables-and-gauge]]. Equality of its actual curvature
with $R^{\mathrm{pre}}$ is the curvature constraint, rather than an assumption
on the independent unknowns. Reduced evolution enforces its time components;
the residual theorem establishes the remaining components from constrained
initial data. This distinction keeps the tentative connection available before
torsion-freeness and the full curvature constraint are proved.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
signature $(-+++)$ and metric-selected connection $\nabla$. Fix mathematical
parameters $c>0$, $\kappa>0$ and $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$. On an open set
$U_0\subseteq M$, prescribe a smooth function $\rho\ge0$ and a smooth
future-directed unit timelike field $u$, with $g(u,u)=-1$. Set
$\varepsilon:=\rho c^2$ and $T^{ab}:=\varepsilon u^au^b$. On the open positive
subset $\{\rho>0\}$, the tuple $(\varepsilon,u)$, rather than $(\rho,u)$, is
exactly the dust model of [[def-gr-dust-matter-model]]: that supplier's density
is the coefficient of $u\otimes u$. Here $\rho$ denotes its mass-normalized
parameter and $\varepsilon$ its energy-normalized coefficient. On zero-density
regions the smooth unit field is prescribed separately; the geodesic equation
is imposed there as well and is not deduced from conservation of the zero
tensor. This is the smooth geodesic-dust extension, without a free boundary
or a division by density. Make the following
**reduction conventions**, all local to an open set $\mathcal U\subseteq U_0$:

**(a) Signature flip.** Put $\gamma:=-g$, a smooth metric of signature
$(+---)$ on $\mathcal U$, with inverse $\gamma^{-1}=-g^{-1}$; all indices in the
reduction are raised and lowered with $\gamma$
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]). Put
$$U:=u,\qquad r:=\rho c^2 .$$
Then $\gamma(U,U)=1$. Whenever the mathematical model equation
$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds, it reads
$G(\gamma)-\Lambda\gamma=\kappa\,r\,U^\flat_\gamma\otimes U^\flat_\gamma$ with
the same constant $\kappa$ and the Einstein tensor of $\gamma$
([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Indeed the constant metric
flip leaves the connection and mixed curvature unchanged, so Ricci is unchanged,
the scalar changes sign and $G(\gamma)=G(g)$; both lower factors in $T$
change sign together. The original metric is recovered by $g=-\gamma$.
Physical identification of these mathematical parameters is made by the
consuming physical model, not assumed by this definition.

**(b) Orthonormal frame.** Choose a smooth orthonormal frame
$(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ on $\mathcal U$ with $e_0=U$ and
$\gamma(e_i,e_j)=\eta_{ij}:=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)_{ij}$
([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]], [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).
Its connection coefficients are defined by
$$\nabla_ie_j=\Gamma_i{}^k{}_j\,e_k,\qquad \Gamma_{ijk}:=\gamma_{kl}\Gamma_i{}^l{}_j=-\Gamma_{ikj},$$
and the frame components of $U$ are $U^i=\delta^i_0$.
The **spatial projection** onto the $\gamma$-orthogonal complement of $U$ and the tensor
$$h_{ij}:=\gamma_{ij}-U_iU_j,\qquad l_{ij}:=h_{ij}-U_iU_j$$
coincide with $\gamma$-orthogonal projection onto $\operatorname{span}(e_1,e_2,e_3)$
when restricted to spatial pairs.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold with
metric-selected connection $\nabla$
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]), and let
$R$ be its curvature ([[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]). Let
$I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an interval with nonempty interior
([[def-interval]]) and let $\gamma:I\to M$ be an affinely parametrized
geodesic with $D_s\gamma'=0$, written $T:=\gamma'$
([[def-geodesic-of-an-affine-connection]]); the parameter is the affinely
parametrized one of that definition and need not be proper time.

**(b) Jacobi field.** A **Jacobi field along $\gamma$** is a smooth field $J$
along $\gamma$ satisfying the **Jacobi equation**
$$D_s^2J=R(T,J)T\qquad(s\in I),$$
that is $D_s^2J=R(\gamma',J)\gamma'$. The assignment
$J\mapsto R(T,J)T$, which associates with a field along $\gamma$ another
field along $\gamma$ and is $\mathbb R$-linear, is the **Jacobi operator of
$\gamma$**. Whether the field is smooth only piecewise is stated whenever a
statement uses piecewise fields; the unqualified term means globally smooth.

**(e) The normal bundle.** If $\gamma$ is future timelike with
$g(T,T)=-1$, define its **normal bundle** to be the vector subbundle
$$N_\gamma:=\bigsqcup_{s\in I}N_\gamma(s)\subseteq\gamma^*TM,\qquad N_\gamma(s):=\{v\in T_{\gamma(s)}M:g_{\gamma(s)}(v,T(s))=0\}.$$
A **normal field** is a smooth section $J$ of $N_\gamma$, equivalently a
smooth field along $\gamma$ satisfying $g(J,T)=0$. Each fibre $N_\gamma(s)$
has dimension three, the restriction of $g_{\gamma(s)}$ to it is positive
definite, and $D_s$ maps normal fields to normal fields, since
$\frac{d}{ds}g(J,T)=g(D_sJ,T)+g(J,D_sT)=g(D_sJ,T)$ and $D_sT=0$; these
facts are proved in [[lem-gr-normal-index-form-factorization]] clause (b).
The norm of a normal field is $|J(s)|:=\sqrt{g_{\gamma(s)}(J(s),J(s))}$.
For any field $V$ along $\gamma$, its **normal component** is the field
$$V^\perp(s):=V(s)+g_{\gamma(s)}(V(s),T(s))\,T(s).$$
Indeed $g(T,T)=-1$ implies $g(V^\perp,T)=0$ and
$V=V^\perp-g(V,T)T$.

- **Observer.** An observer at $p$ is one future-directed unit timelike vector
  $n\in T_pM$, $g_p(n,n)=-1$
  ([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). It carries no parametrized curve and no
  clock reading by itself.
- **Congruence.** An observer congruence on an open set $U$ is a smooth field
  $n$ whose value at every point is an observer; its maximal integral curves
  are its observer curves, and its flow parameter is not a physical time
  ([[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]).
- **Frame and coordinate frame.** A local frame field is a tuple of four
  pointwise independent smooth vector fields; the coordinate frame of a smooth
  chart is the special case of the fields $\partial/\partial x^a$, whose
  members pairwise commute. A frame whose members do not commute is therefore
  not the coordinate frame of any chart
  ([[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]).
- **Tetrad.** A tetrad field is a pointwise $g$-orthonormal frame field; it is
  future-directed when its first member is future-directed, and it is adapted
  to a congruence $n$ when that first member equals $n$. A tetrad field need
  not be a coordinate frame. Local existence near every point is proved on this
  page; global existence on $M$ is not asserted and would be a nontrivial
  parallelizability property of the manifold.
- **Adapted chart.** A chart is $n$-adapted when its spatial coordinates are
  constant along the integral curves of $n$; one exists near every point of a
  congruence, by the existence corollary on this page, but it is not unique and
  its coordinate field need not equal $n$
  ([[cor-gr-adapted-chart-existence]]).
- **Rest spaces and their integrability.** The rest spaces $n_q^{\perp}$ of a
  congruence always form a smooth rank-$3$ distribution, and they are tangent
  to local hypersurfaces exactly when $\alpha\wedge d\alpha=0$ for
  $\alpha=n^{\flat}$. Thus an adapted chart always exists, while an orthogonal
  rest-space foliation need not
  ([[prop-gr-rest-space-integrability-criterion]]).
- **Components.** Coordinate components of a tensor field transform by
  products of chart Jacobians
  ([[lem-gr-tensor-component-transformation-law]]), while its components in
  two future-directed tetrads are related by a matrix
  $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda^{\mathsf T}\eta\Lambda=\eta$ and
  $\Lambda^0{}_0>0$ ([[lem-gr-tetrad-change-of-basis-is-lorentz]]). The two
  component systems are different data
  ([[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]]).
- **Observer-relative quantities.** Observer energy, spatial momentum and
  rest mass are defined with respect to a chosen observer; different observers
  generally assign different energies to the same tangent vector, and no
  observer-independent split of a tangent vector into energy and momentum is
  asserted ([[def-gr-observer-relative-energy-and-momentum]]).
- **Physical readings.** The interpretation of these geometric objects as
  observers, reference frames, clocks, particles and measured energies belongs
  to the physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework, recorded
  elsewhere on this track; the items on this page assert no measurement,
  dynamics or claim about nature.
